finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: ALGO_TEXT[1] is populated with user input or data that can be influenced by an attacker.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
1) The sink is printf, which only outputs to stdout; it does not invoke a shell or execute commands, so OS command injection is not possible.
2) The format string is a compile‑time constant; the user data is supplied as a %s argument, not as part of the format string, preventing format‑string attacks.
3) The code fragment does not show ALGO_TEXT[1] being populated from any untrusted source; without evidence that it contains attacker‑controlled data, the premise of the finding is unsupported.

finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: DESCRIPTION_TEXT[0] is populated with user input or data that can be influenced by an attacker.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked that the sink is printf, which only writes to stdout and does not invoke a shell or execute commands. Therefore even if DESCRIPTION_TEXT[0] contains shell metacharacters, they are not interpreted as commands. No other checks or sanitization are required for command injection. The code does not call system(), exec*, popen(), or similar functions that would execute the string. Hence the reported OS Command Injection is not applicable.
